speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; can you describe exactly how the dizziness feels, such as whether the room is spinning or if you just feel unsteady?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis.

The constant rotational vertigo, nausea, and lack of response to diphenhydramine (which suggests a central component or severe vestibular dysfunction) are classic for vestibular neuritis. I am not attributing the garlic intake to the cause, as it is unlikely to induce such severe symptoms. Given the duration since this morning, I will not order further imaging as this is likely an acute, self-limiting inflammatory process of the vestibular nerve. Do you have any history of recent viral infections or ear pain?
